svg.text: [*] Two speeds: at some points the samples ran at two clearly different speeds, so the line splits in two there. The rarer speed is drawn fainter,
in proportion to how rarely it occurred. A common cause is a chip with performance cores and slower efficiency cores: the operating system runs the work
on either kind. Two copies sharing one unit of the chip, and a virtual machine whose host moves it between cores, split speeds too.

g.data-summary: what each dot shape's code path is, contender by contender
g.text: ▾ Code paths — what each dot shape's code path is, contender by contender

svg.text: BLAKE3 · One message per call · portable compression from the start: Fewer than four whole chunks: each runs through the portable single-chunk compressor, so 2 KiB and 3 KiB take
BLAKE3 · One message per call · NEON hash_many (4-way) from 4 KiB: Four whole chunks fill a NEON batch; from here the bulk of the input runs four chunks at a time.
BLAKE3 · Many 64-byte messages per call · portable compression · one 64 B message per call from the start: Every message is its own call of the one-message entry point; the batch
size changes nothing in the code path.
SHA-256 · One message per call · sha2 aarch64_sha2 backend (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions) from the start: One kernel at every size.
SHA-256 · Many 64-byte messages per call · sha2 aarch64_sha2 backend (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions) · one 64 B message per call from the start: Every message is its own call of the
one-message entry point; the batch size changes nothing in the code path.
SHA-1DC · One message per call · SHA-1 with collision detection, pure Rust from the start: One kernel at every size.
SHA-1DC · Many 64-byte messages per call · SHA-1 with collision detection, pure Rust · one 64 B message per call from the start: Every message is its own call of the one-message
entry point; the batch size changes nothing in the code path.
BLAKE3 servil · One message per call · scalar kernel c1, one call from the start: Inputs of one chunk (1 KiB) or less run every block, the root compression included, in one call
to the integer-only kernel, with the state in registers throughout.
BLAKE3 servil · One message per call · integer + NEON hybrid kernels from 1025 B: Above one chunk the tree is hashed several chunks at a time; below a full SME2 group of sixteen,
the hybrid kernels run scalar chunks on the integer units beside NEON chunks, up to fifteen per call.
BLAKE3 servil · One message per call · SME2 hash16_chunks kernel from 16 KiB: Sixteen whole chunks fill one group on 512-bit streaming vectors, up to eight groups per call; a
remainder below sixteen stays on the hybrid kernels.
BLAKE3 servil · Many 64-byte messages per call · scalar kernel c1, one message per call from the start: A single message runs the same one-call kernel as hash().
BLAKE3 servil · Many 64-byte messages per call · NEON hybrid parent kernels p8/p4/p2 + k1 from 128 B: Two or more one-block messages are compressed together on the NEON hybrid
kernels, up to eight lanes beside a scalar lane per call; on SME2 this remains the path for the messages left over below a group of sixteen.
BLAKE3 servil · Many 64-byte messages per call · SME2 hash16_parents kernel from 1 KiB: Sixteen one-block messages fill one group on 512-bit streaming vectors, one compression per
lane, up to 64 groups per entry into streaming mode; a remainder below sixteen stays on the hybrid kernels.
SHA-256 ring · One message per call · sha256_block_data_order_hw (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions, pipelined schedule) from the start: One kernel at every size.
SHA-256 ring · Many 64-byte messages per call · sha256_block_data_order_hw (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions, pipelined schedule) · one 64 B message per call from the start: Every
message is its own call of the one-message entry point; the batch size changes nothing in the code path.
BLAKE3 mt · One message per call · caller's thread (below one SIMD width of chunks) from the start: One SIMD width of chunks or less is one hash_many call; update_rayon has
BLAKE3 mt · One message per call · rayon::join over the pool from 8 KiB: Above one SIMD width of chunks the tree splits recursively with rayon::join, and idle pool threads steal
BLAKE3 servil mt · One message per call · scalar kernel c1, one call from the start: Inputs of one chunk (1 KiB) or less run every block, the root compression included, in one
call to the integer-only kernel, with the state in registers throughout.
BLAKE3 servil mt · One message per call · integer + NEON hybrid kernels from 1025 B: Above one chunk the tree is hashed several chunks at a time; below a full SME2 group of
sixteen, the hybrid kernels run scalar chunks on the integer units beside NEON chunks, up to fifteen per call.
BLAKE3 servil mt · One message per call · SME2 hash16_chunks kernel from 16 KiB: Sixteen whole chunks fill one group on 512-bit streaming vectors, up to eight groups per call; a
remainder below sixteen stays on the hybrid kernels.
BLAKE3 servil mt · One message per call · subtrees over threads from 64 KiB: From here calls may cut the input at subtree boundaries into pieces of 8 KiB to 128 KiB, shrinking
toward the end, that the calling thread and this crate's worker threads (one per CPU beyond the first) hash at once, each on the NEON hybrid kernels, which run at full speed on
every core at once; the caller merges the chaining values. Concurrent callers' pieces are served in turn; when callers already fill the CPUs, a new call hashes its input whole
BLAKE3 servil mt · Many 64-byte messages per call · scalar kernel c1, one message per call from the start: A single message runs the same one-call kernel as hash().
BLAKE3 servil mt · Many 64-byte messages per call · NEON hybrid parent kernels p8/p4/p2 + k1 from 128 B: Two or more one-block messages are compressed together on the NEON hybrid
kernels, up to eight lanes beside a scalar lane per call; on SME2 this remains the path for the messages left over below a group of sixteen.
BLAKE3 servil mt · Many 64-byte messages per call · SME2 hash16_parents kernel from 1 KiB: Sixteen one-block messages fill one group on 512-bit streaming vectors, one compression
per lane, up to 64 groups per entry into streaming mode; a remainder below sixteen stays on the hybrid kernels.
BLAKE3 servil mt · Many 64-byte messages per call · message ranges over threads from 64 KiB: From here a batch is cut into ranges of messages of 8 KiB to 128 KiB, shrinking toward
the end, that the calling thread and this crate's worker threads hash at once, each range on the NEON hybrid kernels, which run at full speed on every core at once. Concurrent
callers' ranges are served in turn; when callers already fill the CPUs, a new call hashes its batch whole on its own thread.
ab-blake3 · One message per call · const_hash (const fn reference tree, portable compression) from the start: One kernel at every size: a const fn has no run-time SIMD dispatch.
ab-blake3 · Many 64-byte messages per call · single_block_hash_many_exact::<N>, one compression per block from the start: Below sixteen messages the batch entry point compresses
each block on its own; the messages queue through one compression function.
ab-blake3 · Many 64-byte messages per call · single_block_hash_many_exact::<N>, NEON hash_many (4-way) per sixteen blocks from 1 KiB: From sixteen messages each full group of
sixteen blocks goes through the blake3 crate's SIMD hash_many, several blocks per instruction; blocks past the last full group are compressed one at a time.
